# `connectors`

Generated by `connectors-docs` from the definition the `connectors` binary parses: the command tree that ESS generates from the CLI binding [`apps/connectors/spec/cli.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/connectors/blob/main/apps/connectors/spec/cli.yaml), as [`apps/connectors/src/help.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/connectors/blob/main/apps/connectors/src/help.rs) presents it. It lists only commands that exist. `connectors --version` prints the version, and `--help` after any command prints its usage.

> Local integration access through explicitly configured connector instances. After an upgrade, `connectors setup owner-stop` stops the owner an older binary started

## Global options

Every command accepts these, anywhere on the command line.

| Argument | Required | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--config <global_config>` | no | none | any |  |
| `--state-dir <global_state>` | no | none | any |  |
| `--output <global_output>` | no | `human` | `human`, `json` |  |

| [`connectors approvals key-status`](#connectors-approvals-key-status) | Observe public key metadata without starting services or reading secrets |
| [`connectors approvals policy-set`](#connectors-approvals-policy-set) | Publish the exact permitted write-operation set under revision control |
| [`connectors approvals policy-status`](#connectors-approvals-policy-status) | Inspect retained local write policy without starting services |
| [`connectors approvals prepare`](#connectors-approvals-prepare) | Resolve the exact approval subject without provider or credential access |
| [`connectors connections connect`](#connectors-connections-connect) | Begin admitted local protected credential acquisition on <connector>/<instance>; --endpoint first writes that instance's endpoint into the configuration |
| [`connectors connections describe`](#connectors-connections-describe) | Inspect safe metadata for one connection |
| [`connectors connections launch`](#connectors-connections-launch) | Run a pinned consumer with one connection's credential on descriptor 3 |
| [`connectors connections list`](#connectors-connections-list) | List safe connection metadata |
| [`connectors connections reconnect`](#connectors-connections-reconnect) | Publish a new credential on the exact connection without changing its identity; `connections repair` is its deprecated name |
| [`connectors connections repair`](#connectors-connections-repair) | Deprecated name of `connectors connections reconnect` |
| [`connectors connections revalidate`](#connectors-connections-revalidate) | Revalidate the saved credential without re-entry |
| [`connectors connections revoke`](#connectors-connections-revoke) | Commit terminal local revocation under the current fence |
| [`connectors connections status`](#connectors-connections-status) | Observe exactly one connection or acquisition |
| [`connectors connections token`](#connectors-connections-token) | Issue a current access token of one OAuth2 connection, printed only with --reveal |
| [`connectors definitions install`](#connectors-definitions-install) | Fetch the connectors-definitions release TAG from SOURCE (an https repository URL or a local directory), check every file against its index.json, and record it in definitions.lock and a read-only cache; grants nothing and starts no process |
| [`connectors instances describe`](#connectors-instances-describe) | Inspect one configured instance and its cached descriptor; `adapters describe` is its deprecated name |
| [`connectors instances list`](#connectors-instances-list) | List configured instances; `adapters list` is its deprecated name |
| [`connectors instances status`](#connectors-instances-status) | Observe the lifecycle owner of the process that serves one instance; `adapters status` is its deprecated name |
| [`connectors instances stop`](#connectors-instances-stop) | Stop only the exact owned incarnation of the process that serves one instance; `adapters stop` is its deprecated name |
| [`connectors invoke`](#connectors-invoke) | Invoke one operation of a connector's instance; the instance, connection, schema and revision default to the only ones that fit |
| [`connectors list`](#connectors-list) | List every connector this build ships, with its auth profiles and the instances the configuration names; needs no configuration and starts no process |
| [`connectors operations describe`](#connectors-operations-describe) | Inspect an operation and its exact schema identity |
| [`connectors operations list`](#connectors-operations-list) | List operations from selected cached metadata |
| [`connectors setup check`](#connectors-setup-check) | Check local configuration and prerequisites without authentication |
| [`connectors setup checkpoints-enable`](#connectors-setup-checkpoints-enable) | Enable durable open checkpoints on the existing store; one-way, connectors 0.32.0 and earlier can no longer open it |
| [`connectors setup init`](#connectors-setup-init) | Create private local configuration without starting services |
| [`connectors setup migrate`](#connectors-setup-migrate) | Rewrite each entry of the legacy configuration format that maps to a shipped connector as that connector's instance, keeping its instance id, revision and selection; --mode dry-run (or --dry-run) prints the new file, --mode apply (or --apply) writes it and keeps the old one as config.toml.before-migrate-TIMESTAMP (UTC) |
| [`connectors setup owner-stop`](#connectors-setup-owner-stop) | Stop this state directory's running owner, of any build, within 30 seconds; run it after an upgrade when a command answers next_action stop_owner |
| [`connectors completions`](#connectors-completions) | Emit shell completions |

## `connectors invoke`

Invoke one operation of a connector's instance; the instance, connection, schema and revision default to the only ones that fit

```text
connectors invoke [OPTIONS] [CONNECTOR[/INSTANCE]] <OPERATION>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<CONNECTOR[/INSTANCE]>` | no | none | any | The connector, and after one `/` its instance; the instance may be left out when the connector has only one; with --definition the target may be left out, the file naming the connector |
| `<OPERATION>` | yes | none | any | The operation to invoke |
| `--connection <field:connection>` | no | none | any | The connection to invoke through; the instance's only usable one when left out |
| `--schema <field:schema>` | no | none | any | A pin: the operation's schema identity, refused when the current description differs; taken from it when left out |
| `--revision <field:revision>` | no | none | any | A pin: the description's revision, refused when the current description differs; taken from it when left out |
| `--input-json <source:input:inline>` | no | none | any | The input document, as JSON text |
| `--input-file <source:input:file>` | no | none | any | A file holding the input document |
| `--input-stdin` | no | `false` | any | Read the input document from standard input, as happens when no input flag is given |
| `--approval-file <field:approval_file>` | no | none | any | The approval proof a write is invoked with |
| `--idempotency-key <field:idempotency_key>` | no | none | any | A write's idempotency key |
| `--definition <field:definition>` | no | none | any | A connectors-definition/1 file to invoke without configuring it; a target, when given, names its connector |
| `--definitions-root <field:definitions_root>` | no | none | any | With --definition: the tree holding its vendored source and shared auth files [default: the parent of the file's directory] |
| `--credential-file <field:credential_file>` | no | none | any | With --definition: the OAuth client file to connect with when the instance has no connection |
| `--describe <field:describe>` | no | none | any | true: print the operation's description, effect, schema and revision, and invoke nothing |

## `connectors list`

List every connector this build ships, with its auth profiles and the instances the configuration names; needs no configuration and starts no process

```text
connectors list [OPTIONS]
```

```text
connectors operations describe [OPTIONS] --operation <field:operation>
```

| `--adapter <ALIAS>` | no | none | any | Deprecated: the alias of a configured entry; select with --connector and --instance |
| `--connector <field:connector>` | no | none | any |  |
| `--instance <field:instance>` | no | none | any |  |
| `--connection <field:connection>` | no | none | any |  |
| `--operation <field:operation>` | yes | none | any |  |

## `connectors setup check`

Check local configuration and prerequisites without authentication

```text
connectors setup check [OPTIONS]
```

## `connectors setup checkpoints-enable`

Enable durable open checkpoints on the existing store; one-way, connectors 0.32.0 and earlier can no longer open it

```text
connectors setup checkpoints-enable [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--confirm <field:confirm>` | no | none | any |  |

## `connectors setup init`

Create private local configuration without starting services

```text
connectors setup init [OPTIONS]
```

## `connectors setup migrate`

Rewrite each entry of the legacy configuration format that maps to a shipped connector as that connector's instance, keeping its instance id, revision and selection; --mode dry-run (or --dry-run) prints the new file, --mode apply (or --apply) writes it and keeps the old one as config.toml.before-migrate-TIMESTAMP (UTC)

```text
connectors setup migrate [OPTIONS] --mode <field:mode>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--mode <field:mode>` | yes | none | any |  |

## `connectors setup owner-stop`

Stop this state directory's running owner, of any build, within 30 seconds; run it after an upgrade when a command answers next_action stop_owner

```text
connectors setup owner-stop [OPTIONS]
```

## `connectors completions`

Emit shell completions

```text
connectors completions [OPTIONS] <shell>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<shell>` | yes | none | `bash` |  |
